abstract: Let $G$ be biplanar and let $Q$ be an induced nine-vertex-critical subgraph of order at most seventeen with $e(Q)\ge6|V(Q)|-20$. We prove that $G$ is nine-colorable if every nonempty exterior set $X$ spans at most $2|X|-1$ edges. The exterior may have arbitrary order and overlapping neighborhoods in $Q$; in particular, every exterior of arboricity at most two is allowed. A minimal uncolorable exterior satisfies $3r-m+\Delta\le8$, reducing it to at most seven vertices. The accepted order-twenty theorem settles the smaller residues. Vertex-criticality lets us choose either a singleton color class or a monochromatic nonedge, providing adaptive list repairs without any seed-specific matching hypotheses. Elementary Hall and degree-choosability arguments handle most remaining exteriors. Sixty positive graph-polynomial coefficients settle the two exceptional families; a standard-library checker verifies them and exhaustively covers all 1,335 labeled six-vertex cases. The arboricity-two subcase needs none of these new coefficients. The theorem applies to the known seventeen-vertex, 82-edge biplanar seed but is independent of its particular structure. It does not assert extension of every prescribed core coloring, allow arbitrary core-edge deletions, or establish that a ten-critical biplanar graph must contain such a dense induced core.
